senses.definition: An institution, building, or room for the exhibition and conservation of important objects, especially works of art.
examples: In the gallery are displayed genuine artifacts dug up from the site, and in the gift shop you can buy a replica as a souvenir.
Some of her work is so impressive that it really ought to be in a gallery.

senses.definition: An establishment that buys, sells, and displays works of art.
examples: Some of her best work can be yours: it is available at a gallery, if you can afford it.

senses.definition: The uppermost seating area projecting from the rear or side walls of a theater, concert hall, or auditorium.
examples: We could afford the less expensive seats in the gallery.

senses.definition: (by extension, metonymic) The spectators at an event, collectively.
examples: The politician was clearly appealing to the gallery

quotes.text: Capello was missing his son's wedding in Milan to take charge – yet his reshaped England team gave him cause for a double celebration as they overturned the odds in front of a delighted Wembley gallery.
quotes.reference: 2011 November 12, “International friendly: England 1-0 Spain”, in BBC Sport:

senses.definition: (law) The part of a courtroom, often elevated and in the rear, where seating for the public audience is facilitated during trial.

quotes.text:
Rose and Valerie, screaming from the gallery
Say he must go free
quotes.reference: 1969, Paul McCartney, “Maxwell's Silver Hammer”, in Abbey Road, performed by The Beatles:

senses.definition: A roofed promenade, especially one extending along the wall of a building and supported by arches or columns on the outer side.
examples: elegant galleries looking out onto manicured gardens

senses.definition: (computing) A browsable collection of images, font styles, etc.
examples: a clip-art gallery in a word processor

senses.definition: (fortification) A covered passage cut through the earth or masonry.
(mining) A level or drive in a mine.
(automotive) A channel that carries engine oil to parts of the engine that need lubrication, such as the main bearings.

quotes.text: At about 2500 r.p.m., as much oil is by-passed through the cooler as the amount delivered to the main gallery and at higher engine speeds the flow through the cooler is appreciably greater.
quotes.reference: 2012, Colin Campbell, The Sports Car: Its design and performance, page 92:

quotes.text: Metal grit from a previous engine failure was lodged in the oil galleries and had come loose upon driving the vehicle.

senses.definition: A part of a light fixture, forming part of its structure and often providing the mounting for the diffuser.
examples: Holonyms: light fixture, light, lamp, fixture

senses.definition: A part of a monocle—a projection off the ring holding the lens—which helps secure the monocle in the eye socket.
examples: adjusting the distance between the bottom gallery and the top gallery

senses.definition: (entomology) The boring trails produced by an insect in wood.
